question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
sql:
WITH order_needs AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(qty) as total_needed
    FROM orderlines
    WHERE order_id = 423
    GROUP BY product_id
),
inventory_sorted AS (
    SELECT i.id, i.location_id, i.product_id, i.purchase_id, i.qty as avail_qty, 
           l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position, p.purchased
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
      AND i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_needs)
),
cumulative AS (
    SELECT *,
           SUM(avail_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, avail_qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_avail
    FROM inventory_sorted
),
pick_allocation AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           o.total_needed,
           c.avail_qty - GREATEST(0, c.cum_avail - o.total_needed) as qty_to_pick
    FROM cumulative c
    JOIN order_needs o ON c.product_id = o.product_id
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, qty_to_pick
FROM pick_allocation
WHERE qty_to_pick > 0
ORDER BY product_id, purchased, avail_qty

WITH order_needs AS (

      AND i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_needs)

    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, avail_qty) as rn
    FROM inventory_sorted

cumulative AS (
    SELECT *,
           SUM(avail_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, avail_qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_avail
    FROM ranked_inv
),
-- For each inventory row, determine how much to pick
-- We need to pick up to total_needed for each product

    SELECT c.*,
           o.total_needed,
           LAG(c.cum_avail) OVER (PARTITION BY c.product_id ORDER BY c.purchased, c.avail_qty) as prev_cum_avail,

    JOIN order_needs o ON c.product_id = o.product_id
    WHERE c.cum_avail <= o.total_needed
       OR (LAG(c.cum_avail) OVER (PARTITION BY c.product_id ORDER BY c.purchased, c.avail_qty) < o.total_needed)
)
SELECT * FROM pick_allocation
